objectives.statement: Identify EF Core as a lightweight, extensible, open-source, cross-platform object-relational mapper for working with databases through .NET objects.
Explain that an EF Core model consists of entity classes and a context object representing a session with the database.
Explain that a DbContext is normally a short-lived unit of work whose lifetime ends when the instance is disposed.
Identify EF Core migrations as incremental updates that keep a database schema synchronized with a changing model while preserving existing data.
Distinguish conventions, data annotations, and the Fluent API as ways to configure and customize the EF Core model.
Explain that exposing a type through a DbSet property includes it in the EF Core model as an entity type.
Explain that EF Core uses strongly typed LINQ queries which a database provider translates into database-specific query language.
Identify tracking as the default behavior for queries that return entity types and explain its relationship to SaveChanges.
Distinguish no-tracking queries as suitable for read-only scenarios because returned entities are not kept in the change tracker.
Explain how change tracking and SaveChanges persist detected additions, modifications, and deletions.
Identify the principal EF Core entity states such as Detached, Unchanged, Added, Deleted, and Modified.
Distinguish common methods that cause entities to become tracked, including Add, Attach, and Update.
Explain that ASP.NET Core dependency injection can manage DbContext instances with a request-oriented lifetime through AddDbContext.
objectives.citation: DbContext in dependency injection for ASP.NET Core

objectives.statement: Diagnose concurrent use of a single DbContext instance as an invalid threading pattern and explain why asynchronous operations must be awaited before reuse.
Explain how EF Core compares a current model with a previous model snapshot to generate migration source files when the model evolves.
Distinguish ExecuteUpdate and ExecuteDelete as direct bulk database operations from the change-tracking SaveChanges approach.
Explain that relationships in EF Core connect entity types through foreign keys and navigation properties in the model.
Explain identity resolution as returning the same entity instance for repeated occurrences of the same entity in a query result when the behavior is enabled.
Identify EF Core Package Manager Console and .NET CLI tools as design-time tools used for migrations and reverse engineering.
Diagnose failing to await an asynchronous EF Core operation before starting another operation on the same context as a source of concurrency errors.
